parole.testo: From Old Danish egn, from Old Norse eign.

parole.significato: a queen dowager; the widow of a king
parole.testo: From enke (“widow”) + dronning (“queen”), literally “widow queen”. The first element enke (“widow”) is from Old Danish ænkia (“widow”), corresponding to Old Norse ekkja (“widow”), from Proto-Germanic *ainakjǭ (“widow”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos (“one”). The second element dronnin
Developed from Old Danish mon, from Old Norse móa (“to digest”), from Proto-Germanic *meuk- or *mūk-, from Proto-Indo-European *mewg- (“slimy, slippery”).

Influenced by Old Danish slenghe and Danish slænge, from Old Norse slængja, slyngja, causative of slængva, sløngva, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *slangwijaną. Compare Norwegian Nynorsk slengja, which retains the diphthong from Old Norse; also Icelandic slengja, Old Swedish slængia → Swedish slänga

parole.significato: drunkard, a person who is constantly out drinking (alcohol)
parole.testo: ture + basse, first part from Old Danish ture (“to go on a warpath or ravage”). Last part from Old Norse bassi (“bear”).
